meta.title: Open Energy Studio — OpenAEC Foundation
meta.description: Open Energy Studio: open-source energy performance software for dwellings and utility buildings under the Dutch NTA 8800 standard. BENG, TOjuli, energy label, survey and tailored advice. For Windows, macOS, Linux and the browser.

header.label: Energy performance · NTA 8800
header.title: Open Energy Studio
header.tagline: Open source calculation of BENG and the energy label
header.desc: The energy performance of dwellings and utility buildings under NTA 8800, with a calculation kernel you can check for yourself. From new builds with BENG 1, 2 and 3 and TOjuli to existing buildings with a survey, tailored advice and relabelling. On the desktop and in the browser.

alt.results: The results page of Open Energy Studio with the energy label, BENG 1, 2 and 3, TOjuli and the monthly energy need of a sample office
alt.envelope: Entering the thermal envelope of a sample dwelling: walls, roofs, floor and windows by orientation, with the provisional result on the right
alt.monthly: The results overview with the energy use per month and the key figures of the calculation

notice.text: Not yet attested. Open Energy Studio does not (yet) hold a BRL 9501 attest. The results are indicative and cannot be used for an official energy label, a BENG check for a permit or registration in EP-Online.

features.label: Features
features.heading: From building envelope to registration file
features.sub: Start with the highlights or pick a topic.

kernel.title: NTA 8800 in an open calculation kernel
kernel.desc: Energy need, BENG 1, 2 and 3, TOjuli, primary fossil energy use and the energy label all come from one calculation kernel written in Rust. Every result carries the kernel version and a fingerprint of the input, and the calculation trace shows where a number comes from.

input.title: Step by step, with the result alongside
input.desc: Project, building, installations, check, results and registration: the app guides you through the calculation in fixed steps. For each calculation zone you enter the surfaces, constructions, thermal bridges and airtightness, and the provisional result updates with every change.

existing.title: Survey, tailored advice and relabelling
existing.desc: Survey existing dwellings and utility buildings following ISSO 82.1 and 75.1 and turn the answers into project input. Build tailored advice with user profiles, fitting to measured consumption, packages of measures and net present value, and compare an original and a changed project when relabelling.

dossier.title: Report, file and integrations
dossier.desc: Produce a report at three levels of detail, attach evidence to the input and export a file with a manifest and a SHA-256 per document. Other programs and AI assistants can calculate along through a local HTTP API and an MCP server.

kernel.title: NTA 8800 kernel
kernel.desc: Energy need, BENG 1/2/3, TOjuli, primary energy and the energy label, deterministic and without I/O.

editions.title: Standard editions
editions.desc: NTA 8800:2025+C1 by default; 2024, 2023, 2022 and 2020+A1 as older editions that cannot be registered.

envelope.title: Envelope and zones
envelope.desc: Walls, roofs, floors and windows per calculation zone, with constructions, thermal bridges, airtightness and unheated spaces.

model3d.title: 3D model
model3d.desc: View the building envelope you entered in 3D.

results.title: Results and calculation trace
results.desc: By service, by zone and by month, with the origin of every number.

survey.title: Survey
survey.desc: Survey of existing dwellings (ISSO 82.1) and utility buildings (ISSO 75.1), converted into project input.

advice.title: Tailored advice
advice.desc: Following ISSO 82.2 and 75.2: user profiles, measured consumption, packages of measures and net present value.

relabel.title: Relabelling
relabel.desc: Compare an original and a changed project following BRL 9500, annexes 6a and 6b.

reports.title: Reports
reports.desc: An energy performance report as a summary, standard or detailed, plus a report for the tailored advice.

evidence.title: Source and evidence
evidence.desc: Evidence linked to the input, including what you take over from the register of a quality declaration.

dossier.title: Registration file
dossier.desc: Registration data, label statements and a ZIP with a manifest and a SHA-256 per file.

eponline.title: EP-Online overview
eponline.desc: The data in the structure of the EP-Online export, with the field limits from the schema.

api.title: HTTP API
api.desc: All 46 kernel operations through a local API with an OpenAPI 3.1 description.

mcp.title: Works with an AI assistant
mcp.desc: An MCP server with the same operations; every tool only calculates and changes nothing.

import.title: Import and export
import.desc: Exchange files from other NTA 8800 software, with the file name, a SHA-256 and the import notes for each import.

web.title: Desktop and browser
web.desc: The same interface on Windows, macOS and Linux, and in the browser with the kernel as WebAssembly, without a server.

manual.title: Manual
manual.desc: A Dutch manual in the app and with every release, stamped for the kernel version.

snap.desc: For Linux there is now also a Snap package, next to .deb, .rpm and AppImage.

cost.a: Nothing. Open Energy Studio is open source under the LGPL-3.0: no licence fees and no account. The texts of NTA 8800, ISSO and BRL are not included; you need your own copies of those.

attest.q: Can I use it for an official energy label?
attest.a: Not yet. The software holds no BRL 9501 attest, so the results are indicative and cannot be used for an energy label, a BENG check for a permit or registration in EP-Online. The goal is a calculation tool that can be attested; what is still open for that is listed requirement by requirement in the repository.

editions.q: Which edition of NTA 8800 does it calculate?
editions.a: NTA 8800:2025+C1:2026 by default. You can also calculate the 2024, 2023, 2022 and 2020+A1 editions, but those cannot be registered. When you switch edition, the app first shows what the new edition refuses or additionally requires.

existing.q: Does it also work for existing buildings?
existing.a: Yes. There is a survey for existing dwellings (ISSO 82.1) and utility buildings (ISSO 75.1), tailored advice following ISSO 82.2 and 75.2, and relabelling following BRL 9500.

web.q: What is the difference between the web version and the desktop app?
web.a: Both have the same interface and the same kernel. In the browser the kernel runs as WebAssembly on your own computer, without a server. The desktop app saves projects as files and tells you itself when a new version is out.

verify.q: How do I know the calculation is right?
verify.a: Every change to the kernel has to pass a fixed gate: tests with values calculated from the standard's pages independently of the code, public calculation reports and the RVO reference dwellings. In the app the calculation trace shows where every number comes from.

import.q: Can I import projects from other software?
import.a: Yes, through exchange files from other NTA 8800 software. Every import records the file name, a SHA-256 and a list of import notes. Before registration you confirm yourself that you have checked the imported data.

versions.q: How often is there a new version?
versions.a: Regularly, as preview releases. The version number is year, week and sequence number, such as 2026.45.0; the kernel has its own version, which is stamped on every result. The download buttons on this page point to the newest release.
